get.summary:
The My organizations table: every organization the viewer belongs to with its
owner, agent and member counts and its recorded usage. Aggregating the usage
costs more than the plain list, so only that table asks for it.

delete.summary:
Delete an organization as its owner. Every member leaves with it and its
invitations, shared-agent links and recorded usage are removed. The
Workspace connections behind the shared agents are not touched.

204.description: Organization deleted with its memberships, invitations, agent links and recorded usage

parameters.description: Fetch live provider quota metrics; defaults to false

post.summary:
Link an owned Workspace connection into an organization. The organization
agent is the same connection and credential, not a copy. Repeating the
request, including concurrently, returns the existing link.

200.description: Owned agent was already linked; the existing link is returned

201.description: Owned agent linked to the organization

put.summary:
Make an organization the viewer's default, the one their Organization pages
open with. Only an accepted member can, and the previous default stops being
one. Repeating the request changes nothing.

AccountCounts.description: How many accounts there are in each standing, under the search.

accounts.description: Newest first, at most 1,000. A collaborator sees the ones they loaded.

AccountPage.description: One page of accounts, and what the search finds in all.

counts.description: How many accounts each standing has under the search, whichever is shown.

total.description: How many the standing and the search match, across every page.

available.description: The count of the package now.

email_hint.description:
The account as a page lists it now: the email hidden but for its first
letter and its domain.

added.description: Lines that were not among `ids`, put in stock.

available.description: The count of the package after the edit.

changed.description: Accounts whose line is not what it was.

duplicates.description: Lines left out because the package already holds exactly that account.

removed.description: Accounts taken out of stock because their line is gone from the block.

available.description: The count of the package now: the accounts not yet sold.

duplicates.description: Lines left out because the package already holds exactly that account.

username.description: The username of an account that already exists.

validation_url.description:
The provider's own account-verification link while this account needs
its owner to verify it, such as a Google Code Assist challenge.

The provider's own account-verification link while this account needs
its owner to verify it.

audience.description:
How many chats the bot is sending it to. They are sent one by one, at a
pace Telegram allows, so this is how many it has started on.

channel.description: Whether the channel got it. False when no channel is set, or it refused.

product.description:
The slug of a package. Naming one adds a "Mua ngay" button that opens
that package in the bot; without it the message goes out bare.

text.description: Plain text, up to 4,096 characters. The bot sends it as it is.

connection_id.description: The account that is sold, verified again as the ticket is made.

days.description: How long the key lasts once it is bought, 1 to 365.

CreateProduct.description: What a person types into the form; the slug is made from it, once.

available.description:
The count to start from, 0 to 1,000,000. Always 0 for a package that
hands out accounts.

delivers_accounts.description:
Hands the buyer an account when they have paid, from accounts loaded
with `POST .../accounts`. It can be changed later with `PUT .../{slug}`.

warranty_note.description:
The warranty note a buyer reads, up to 200 characters. Blank or absent
uses the standard note for the warranty code.

DashboardListing.description: A ticket that has not been sold: for sale, or kept off sale until its owner fixes it.

days.description: How long the key lasts once it is bought.

listed.description: Whether it is switched on for sale.

quota.description:
What the account had left when it was verified; empty when the provider does
not say.

seller.description: The username of the member of staff who put it on sale.

status.description:
`for_sale`, `hidden` (switched off), `needs_reconnect` (its owner has to
connect the account again) or `disconnected` (the account is gone).

customer_username.description: The buyer's Telegram name, when they have one.

expires_at.description: Past this the order no longer holds stock, but it can still be paid.

handled_by.description:
The username of the member of staff who marked it paid or cancelled it.
Empty for an order SePay settled, and one the buyer cancelled.

payment_method.description: `bank_transfer`, `usdt` or `cash`; set once the order is paid.

counts.description: How many orders each status has under the search, whatever status is shown.

total.description: How many orders the status and the search match, across every page.

DashboardProduct.description:
A product as the dashboard shows it: the catalogue's fields that a page uses,
with the count split three ways.

available.description: What a buyer may still order: `on_hand` less `reserved`.

delivers_accounts.description:
Hands the buyer an account when they have paid. Its count is the number
of accounts not yet sold, so it cannot be changed by hand.

on_hand.description: The count the shop set, before reservations.

reserved.description: Held by orders that await payment and have not expired.

slug.description: The identity of the product; it never changes, whatever the name does.

warranty.description: `WF` full, `W7D` seven days, `NW` none beyond a one-hour login check.

warranty_note.description:
The shop's own warranty note, in Vietnamese. Absent when the product
carries the standard note for its warranty code.

by_seller.description: By what they came to, over the period shown.

daily.description:
Every day of the period and of the one before it, oldest first, with the
days that took nothing present as zero. That is `2 * days` entries, so the
page can set a period against the one before.

top_items.description: By how many orders, over the period shown.

sellers.description:
Every member of staff who has marked an order paid, by username, so the
history can be narrowed to one of them. It does not depend on the filters.

total.description: How many paid orders match, across every page.

total_vnd.description: What they come to, in đồng, across every page.

cached_micro_per_million.description: Micro-dollars for a million cached input tokens.

input_micro_per_million.description: Micro-dollars for a million new input tokens.

listed.description: Whether customers can use it; an unlisted model is refused.

model.description: The id the agent's API uses.

name.description: What the Pricing page calls it.

output_micro_per_million.description: Micro-dollars for a million output tokens.

position.description: Among its agent's models, smallest first.

permissions.description: What the role may open, so the page can hide a link the API would refuse.

key_last_four.description: The last four characters of the key the customer got.

price_micro.description: What the customer paid, in micro-dollars.

EditAccounts.description: Accounts the owner opened, and the block they left them as. Not `Debug`.

accounts.description:
One account per line, `email|password`, as the owner left the block; blank
lines are skipped. Empty takes every account in `ids` out of stock.

dry_run.description: Report what would change and change nothing.

ids.description: The accounts the block was made from, all unsold and all of this package.

completed_requests.description: Requests the provider finished; the rest were abandoned or failed.

spent_micro.description:
What the requests were charged to the service wallet, in micro-dollars;
zero for the Workspace, whose requests are free.

gateway_key_id.description:
The Hub key that sent the requests; none for the Playground, or for a
key that has since been deleted.

spent_micro.description:
What these requests were charged to the service wallet, in micro-dollars;
zero for the Workspace, whose requests are free.

LoadAccounts.description:
A block of accounts to load. It is not `Debug` on purpose: a derived
`Debug` would print the accounts wherever the request is logged.

accounts.description:
One account per line, `email|password`: at most 1,000 lines of at most 300
characters. Blank lines are skipped and the spaces around the bar are dropped.

is_default.description:
The organization the viewer's Organization pages open with. At most one
organization is the default; creating or joining one, or choosing it,
makes it the default, and leaving it or its deletion clears that.

validation_url.description:
The provider's own account-verification link while this account needs
its owner to verify it.

id.description: The Hub user ID, also used by the Usage member_id filter.

OrganizationSummary.description:
An organization the viewer belongs to, with what the My organizations table
shows: the owner, the agent and member counts, and recorded usage over the
last `period_days` UTC days (the same figures its Overview reports).

is_default.description: Whether this is the organization the viewer's Organization pages open with.

OwnedTicket.description: A ticket the signed-in user bought, without its key.

key_id.description: The key's id, for replacing it.

payment_method.description: How the money reached the shop.

PaymentMethod.description:
How an order was paid. SePay settles a bank transfer by itself; the rest is
something a member of staff saw and recorded.

Permission.description: What a page or an endpoint asks of a role.

connection_id.description:
The account to try first. A Service chat has none: the platform's stock
serves it.

service.description: Chat in the Service's scope: charged to the wallet, served by the stock.

PurchasedTicket.description: A ticket's key, shown once, with what it is for.

key.description: The key, which is never shown again.

QuotaMetric.description: One line of what an account has left, as the provider reports it.

platform.description: `x`, `twitter`, `tiktok` or `facebook`; detected from the link when omitted.

url.description: Link to one public video or reel.

RevealAccounts.description:
The owner's password, to show the owner is who they say, and the accounts to
open. Not `Debug`, for the same reason as an account.

ids.description: At least one and at most 1,000; each is opened once, in this order.

RevealedAccounts.description: The accounts asked for, in the clear. Not `Debug`.

seller.description: The username of the member of staff, or empty for what SePay settled.

Role.description: What a member of staff is, in the dashboard.

model.description:
The id the agent's API uses. A model that has a row is changed, any other
is added.

input_micro_per_million.description: Micro-dollars (1 USD = 1,000,000) per one million tokens.

card_top_up.description: Whether a top-up is paid by card, through Stripe Checkout.

min_balance_micro.description:
A request starts only when the wallet holds at least this much, since what
it costs is known only when it ends. Micro-dollars.

test_top_up.description: Whether topping up works without a payment. True on staging only.

available.description:
Whether the platform's stock has an account that can serve this agent now.
When it has none, a request for it answers 502.

checkout_url.description:
Where to send the customer to pay by card. None when the wallet was
credited at once, which only happens where test top-ups are on.

wallet_micro.description:
What the customer holds, in micro-dollars. A payment by card is not in it
until Stripe reports it.
What the customer holds, in micro-dollars.

notified.description: Whether the bot told the buyer. The order is paid either way.

last_active_at.description: When they last signed in, or last had their session refreshed.

locked.description:
The last active owner, whose role cannot change and who cannot be removed,
so the shop is never left without one.

orders_today.description: Orders they marked paid today, in shop time.

revenue_today_vnd.description: What those orders come to, in đồng.

StockAccount.description:
One account as a page lists it. The email is hidden but for its first letter
and its domain, and the password is not here at all.

order_reference.description: The order it was handed to, once it has been.

product_slug.description: The package it belongs to, by its slug and by its name.

delta.description: Units to put in (up to 100,000) or take out (up to 1,000,000), never 0.

days.description: How long the key lasts once it is bought.

quota.description:
What the account had left when it was put on sale; empty when the provider
does not say.

providers.description: Only the agents that have a ticket for sale, in the order of the Pricing page.

UpdateAccount.description: A new email and/or password for an account. Not `Debug`, like an account.

email.description: A new email. Left out or blank keeps the one it has.

password.description: A new password. Left out or blank keeps the one it has.

listed.description: Whether it is switched on for sale.

UpdateProduct.description:
Everything about a product that can be edited. The slug and the count are not
in it: the slug is the product's identity, and the count has its own change
(a package that hands out accounts counts its accounts instead).

delivers_accounts.description:
Makes the package hand out accounts, or stop. Absent leaves it as it is.
Turning it on makes the count the number of accounts not sold (0 for a
package that never held any), so the count typed in by hand is gone; it is
refused while buyers have orders open. Turning it off is refused while the
package still holds accounts not sold.

warranty_note.description:
The warranty note a buyer reads, up to 200 characters. Blank uses the
standard note for the warranty code. Absent leaves the note as it is,
unless the warranty code changes, which resets it to the standard one.

quota.description: What the account has left, as the provider says; empty when it does not.

connection_id.description: An account the signed-in member connected, on the Agents page or from here.
